electrons, that travel in the electrolytic bath and then on the cathode they combine the
electrons with copper ions and form copper on the surface, cooper electroplating can
have many variables, temperature, resistance of the anode, voltage, current, quality of
the electricity, and many others that influence the quality, thickness, surface and time,
but on this experiment I will be focusing on one dependant and an independent
variable, the dependant being the thickness of the layer formed on the cube, and the
independent variable being the input electricity, in this case I will maintain the watts
always the same, but the voltage and current will be modulated.

Results

The first voltage was 1 and 0.5 amps while the second 0.250 amps and 2 v, getting 1 watt
